title: Robbins' theorem on diconnected orientations
statement: Let $G$ be a finite simple graph on a nonempty vertex set, and suppose its edge connectivity satisfies $\kappa'(G) \ge 2$. Then $G$ has a diconnected orientation: one can assign a direction to each edge of $G$, forming a digraph $D$ whose underlying graph is $G$, so that for every ordered pair of vertices $u, v$ there is a directed path in $D$ from $u$ to $v$.
replaced:
